label: Product
title: People, context,
description: Bring the conversation and the work into one considered workspace. SynqHarbor connects a focused product experience with an open, self-hostable platform roadmap.

sections.title: A place for the whole story
sections.body: Move between conversations, tasks, artifacts and decisions without losing why the work matters.
items: A task board with clear ownership

sections.title: Human direction comes first
sections.body: The product architecture separates a request, an execution attempt, an artifact and authorization. These records have different responsibilities.

label: Solutions
title: Work that fits
description: Client delivery, team operations and content work benefit from shared context, visible ownership and thoughtful review.

sections.title: Client delivery
sections.body: Keep the request, acceptance criteria, discussions and deliverables connected. The target workflow gives clients content review while developers retain release authority.

sections.title: Team operations
sections.body: Turn commitments into visible work. The planned operations layer connects approved sources and prepares follow-up material for human review.

sections.title: Content and ideas
sections.body: Keep research, drafts and brand guidance close to the work. Publishing belongs to a separately authorized integration.

label: Agents
title: Clear roles.
description: Builder and Reviewer are the initial role model. Runtime, provider, permissions and execution location remain separate design decisions.

sections.title: Builder
sections.body: A focused executor receives a bounded task, acceptance criteria and a permission scope. Work produces versioned artifacts rather than an unsupported success claim.

sections.title: Reviewer
sections.body: Review checks the exact artifact and retained evidence. A second model alone does not establish correctness; protected tests and human judgment remain necessary.

sections.title: Execution availability
sections.body: Agent profiles are part of the current interface. Provider execution, subscriptions, coding runners and scheduled agent jobs are not connected in this website release.
items: No provider credentials are sent to the browser

label: Integrations
title: Connect the context.
description: The integration roadmap prioritizes one qualified connector at a time, explicit permissions and recoverable external actions.

sections.title: Tools and knowledge
sections.body: MCP is a planned tool-connection interface. Every call must still pass application authorization and scoped credential checks.
items: Read grants separated from write grants
Search and downloads share the same authorization rules

sections.title: Code delivery
sections.body: Repository access, isolated execution and publishing authority are separate capabilities. Native coding-agent adapters require provider-specific qualification.

sections.title: Connection status
sections.body: No third-party accounts or providers are connected by this website. The current release has no paid API runtime or automatic external publication.

label: Self-hosting
title: Your infrastructure.
description: The website ships as a static Next.js export. The platform roadmap keeps the authenticated core and execution workers under explicit operator ownership.

sections.title: Deploy the current website
sections.body: Use Node.js 24, install the locked dependencies, configure the public origin, and build. Serve the exported files with a static web server.
items: Serve out/ over HTTPS; preserve actual 404 responses

sections.title: Configuration and recovery
sections.body: The repository documents public configuration separately from secret recovery material. Versioned releases, file manifests and off-server archives support restoration.
items: Verify restored files and live parity

sections.title: Future platform operation
sections.body: FastAPI, PostgreSQL, private object storage and isolated outbound runners form the planned application architecture. Their implementation remains a separate engineering phase.
items: An existing server supports the startup path
AWS/GCP/Azure public surfaces have qualified free options
Large-scale capacity requires measured sizing and approved funding

label: Roadmap
title: A clear course.
accent: One useful release at a time.
description: Ten engineering phases build from a verified foundation to reliable client workflows and operational readiness. Every phase has parallel disciplines and a deployment gate.

sections.title: 01–03 · Establish the foundation
sections.body: Repeatable deployment, secure identity and tenancy, then durable collaboration form the first platform foundation.
items: 03: collaboration, tasks and durable controlled execution

sections.title: 04–07 · Complete the delivery path
sections.body: Versioned artifacts and approval authority precede local execution, client delivery and permission-aware knowledge.
items: 04: artifacts, protected evidence and exact approvals
05: qualified local AI and isolated Builder/Reviewer

sections.title: 08–10 · Make operation repeatable
sections.body: Business workflows, reliability and portability lead to a verified pilot and handover. Expansion follows measured requirements.
items: 08: business workflows, schedules and reusable skills
09: operations, reliability, portability and capacity qualification
10: production pilot, independent audit and handover

label: About
title: Good work deserves
description: SynqHarbor AI is an independent project maintained by Zahidul Islam, designed around human-led collaboration and controlled agent workflows.

sections.title: The problem worth solving
sections.body: Conversation tools, task systems and individual AI sessions often separate the context from the outcome. SynqHarbor aims to reconnect that story.
items: One place for the brief and decisions
A visible path from work to review
A handover another operator can understand

sections.title: The principles
sections.body: Make responsibility clear. Keep permissions explicit. Prefer useful evidence over activity volume. Build portable systems with documented ownership.

sections.title: Follow the work
sections.body: Development and public technical documentation are maintained in the project repository. Feedback can be shared through the contact page.

label: Security
title: Visible controls.
description: Security documentation describes current website controls and the requirements that govern the future authenticated platform.

sections.title: Current website controls
sections.body: The release uses self-hosted assets, HTTPS, a restrictive script policy, dependency scanning and a hardened static server. Secrets and private project records are excluded from publication.
items: Content Security Policy generated from release scripts
No provider credentials in browser code

sections.title: Future application requirements
sections.body: Every resource access must pass tenant and role authorization. Sessions, CSRF, grants, immutable approvals and isolated workers are engineering requirements before real workflow execution.
items: Independent approval actors and exact versions
Bounded tools and revocable connector grants

sections.title: Report a vulnerability
sections.body: Follow SECURITY.md in the repository. Private vulnerability reporting is the preferred channel; do not test unrelated infrastructure or access other people’s data.

label: Architecture
title: A system with clear owners.
description: Next.js exports static routes. React and Motion handle browser interactions. A hardened static server sits behind Caddy HTTPS and Cloudflare delivery. Browser workspace state does not leave the tab.

sections.title: Current website
sections.body: Next.js exports static routes. React and Motion handle browser interactions. A hardened static server sits behind Caddy HTTPS and Cloudflare delivery. Browser workspace state does not leave the tab.

sections.title: Future control plane
sections.body: FastAPI and PostgreSQL own identities, membership, tasks, runs, artifacts, approvals, grants and an append-only application audit trail. A modular monolith keeps one authoritative task dispatcher.

sections.title: Execution boundary
sections.body: Outbound runners accept bounded assignments. Coding work runs in disposable isolated environments; the web server never executes arbitrary agent-generated commands. Tools enforce authorization independently of model output.

label: API roadmap
title: A contract before a connection.
description: The current website has no deployed application API. No account, connector, inference or release request is issued by the browser. The public source documents the future contract.

sections.title: Current interfaces
sections.body: The current website has no deployed application API. No account, connector, inference or release request is issued by the browser. The public source documents the future contract.

sections.title: Planned API domains
sections.body: Identity and sessions; organizations and membership; rooms and messages; tasks and runs; artifacts and approvals; connector grants; usage and schedules. OpenAPI will be generated from implemented routes.

sections.title: Contract requirements
sections.body: Tenant scope and role checks apply to every object access. Unsafe requests require CSRF/origin protection. Input bounds, pagination, optimistic revisions, idempotency and structured errors are part of endpoint acceptance criteria.

label: Security architecture
title: Permissions before prompts.
description: The authenticated phase requires secure server-side sessions, revocation, exact Origin checks, CSRF protection and explicit membership authorization before any object reaches the caller.

sections.title: Identity and tenant boundaries
sections.body: The authenticated phase requires secure server-side sessions, revocation, exact Origin checks, CSRF protection and explicit membership authorization before any object reaches the caller.

sections.title: Artifacts and consequential actions
sections.body: Approvals bind the exact version/hash, destination and arguments. A content change invalidates authorization. Separate actors approve content and release. External writes record intent, idempotency keys and destination receipts.

sections.title: Execution and retrieval
sections.body: Apply permissions before retrieval content reaches a model. Treat retrieved instructions as untrusted. Isolate runners and generated applications, restrict network/filesystem access, and keep provider credentials outside browser code.

label: Scalability
title: A million connections needs a workload.
description: Target one million simultaneously connected users, with an assumed 10% active fraction and 0.2 API requests per active user per second: 20,000 requests/second sustained and 40,000 burst. These are planning assumptions, not test results.

sections.title: Future design envelope
sections.body: Target one million simultaneously connected users, with an assumed 10% active fraction and 0.2 API requests per active user per second: 20,000 requests/second sustained and 40,000 burst. These are planning assumptions, not test results.

sections.title: Architecture stages
sections.body: Progress from a measured single-host core to stateless replicas, bounded connection pools and separate gateways; then regional cells, tenant routing, private object storage and partitioning justified by query evidence.

sections.title: Qualification and funding
sections.body: Test 1K, 10K, 100K and 1M connections with realistic write ratios, tenant skew, reconnect storms and failure recovery. Size services from measured throughput and target utilization. Startup free plans do not fund the full target envelope.

label: Reliability
title: Define the objective. Measure the experience.
description: Proposed website/core availability objective: 99% over rolling 30 days, corresponding to 7h 12m of time-based unavailability. Future multi-zone objective 99.9% corresponds to 43m 12s. These are objectives, not observed history or contractual promises.

sections.title: Initial operating objective
sections.body: Proposed website/core availability objective: 99% over rolling 30 days, corresponding to 7h 12m of time-based unavailability. Future multi-zone objective 99.9% corresponds to 43m 12s. These are objectives, not observed history or contractual promises.

sections.title: Measurement policy
sections.body: Separate website availability, authenticated API success/latency and asynchronous completion. Count eligible timeouts, 5xx and valid-workload 429s as failures. Define maintenance treatment, telemetry gaps and monitoring coverage explicitly.

sections.title: Response and recovery
sections.body: Use public incident communication, error-budget-based prioritization, rollback procedures and postmortems. Backup success must be followed by a timed restore drill and application-level verification.

label: Operations
title: A release another person can operate.
description: Build locally from the lockfile with the intended public origin. Keep versioned releases and content hashes. Validate the project server configuration before atomic activation, preserving unrelated applications.

sections.title: Website deployment
sections.body: Build locally from the lockfile with the intended public origin. Keep versioned releases and content hashes. Validate the project server configuration before atomic activation, preserving unrelated applications.

sections.title: Backup and rollback
sections.body: Retain an off-server release archive and verify extraction against the manifest. Keep a previous release for rollback. The future database phase adds encrypted off-host backups, retention and restore drills before valuable data is accepted.

sections.title: Recovery targets
sections.body: Proposed initial application targets: RPO≤24h and RTO≤8h; later RPO≤15min/RTO≤1h after WAL/PITR and operational qualification. They remain targets until timed restoration evidence is published.
